result.title: Beyond Pose Control: Anatomically Consistent Ultrasound Video Generation
result.summary: Camera-controlled video generation anticipates how a scene appears from new viewpoints by relying on a prior learned implicitly from large-scale data. Ultrasound poses the same problem, with the probe pose as the viewpoint, but under opposite conditions: anatomy offers an explicit prior that every sonographer relies on, whereas tracked scans are too scarce to learn it implicitly. As a result, pose control alone is not enough, and pose-conditioned ultrasound generators produce implausible anatomy in unscanned regions and inconsistent anatomy on revisits. We go beyond pose control and give the generator the two kinds of knowledge that make up a sonographer's mental model. An anatomical prior, built from a population of subjects, guides generation where nothing has been scanned, and is refined online by every generated chunk towards the scanned subject. A 3D latent memory, designed around the cross-sectional physics of ultrasound, compounds the generated slices into a volume of the patient and reslices it at new poses, keeping revisited anatomy consistent. The fine-grained memory enters the generator at the input, while the coarse anatomy prior guides the layout across transformer blocks. Experiments on thyroid, kidney, and lumbar spine show improved visual fidelity, pose following, and anatomical consistency over pose-conditioned and memory-augmented baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向探头位姿可控的超声视频生成，在位姿条件之外引入由人群数据构建、并随每个生成块在线细化的解剖先验，以及按超声断面物理设计的 3D latent memory，将已生成切片累积为患者体数据并在新位姿处重切片，以改善未扫描区域与重复回访时的解剖一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「3D latent memory」作为随生成过程在线更新的持久内部状态、并按新位姿重新取用，可为 LVR 中跨步骤维护与查询 latent 空间状态、以及状态在视角或位置变化下的一致性问题提供方法线索；但该工作目标是逼真视频合成，未涉及证据获取与推理决策，需核查其状态更新与查询机制是否可迁移。
